newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha holds steady in post-Skikda sleepiness.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha holds steady in post-Skikda sleepiness.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices held steady on Tuesday in quiet activity that reflected ambivalence to Skikda loadings and generally neutral local interest that has mirrored sideways crude prices.
Bids and offers in the physical NWE market were wide apart and no deals were heard done, with even less direction coming from traders in the swaps market.
May swaps edged up 50 cents to $180/$181 a tonne with June at $182.50/$183.50 and July valued near $183.
NWE cargoes were notionally set at a small contango to May swaps, near $176/$180 cif, traders said.
"The market is balanced," one broker said. "There is good supply and the buyers are there but not really at attractive numbers."
One trader was heard bidding for 25-30,000 tonne pipeline spec material for the second half of May, and another trader was offering prompt pipeline material, sources said.
One source said another trader was bidding for pipeline spec for the second straight day, but did not appear to want to conclude a deal. Material was also available out of Flushing, he said.
"It's a complete standoff," he said. "It's a combination of crude, where prices are stable, and Europe not being interested in imports from northern Africa."
The arbitrage from the Med to the U.S. could open if the arb was unattractive to the Far East and Europe remained uninterested, he said.
